notes.NC17.1.OA.1: All sums and starting amounts are within 20. Skills: result unknown (3), put together (6), change unknown (5), start unknown (4), compare (7), matching a story to a number sentence (5). Compare is about a quarter because it has three forms (difference, bigger, smaller unknown).
notes.NC17.1.OA.3: Sums are within 20. Grade 1 does not name the properties for students, so the questions test the strategies (turn-around facts, making a ten, adding in a convenient order) and equations showing them. Choice options within each question end the same way. Sums stay within 20. Subtraction is used only in distractors.
notes.NC17.1.OA.4: Sums and totals stay within 20. Adding on and rewriting as subtraction are both asked, plus a first-addend-unknown form and matching a number sentence to a story.
notes.NC17.1.OA.6: Number lines are described in words (start at, jump right or left). Subtraction signs are written as plain hyphens, so no LaTeX is used.
notes.NC17.1.OA.7: Every sum and difference stays within 20. A single equation cannot be a numeric question with a true/false answer, so "is it true" is asked as which-is-true, which-is-not-true and how-many-are-true; missing numbers and stories are numeric.
notes.NC17.1.OA.8: All numbers within 20, plus tens within 100. Skills (counts below in reply).
notes.NC17.1.NBT.1: Counts by ones forward only, with starts below 150 and ends up to 150 (the standard reaches 150, so numbers past 120 are used). Skills: say the next number (7), find the missing number (6), count on a few numbers from a start (6), choose the correct counting list (6), count up to 150 (5). Counting by tens and counting back are other standards.
notes.NC17.1.NBT.7: Numbers stay within 100 as the standard says. Pictures of objects are replaced by bundles, boxes and rows of ten described in words. Number names are only ever given as text, in choice or numeric stems.
notes.NC17.1.NBT.2: Grade 1 only: numbers kept within 100, whole-number answers. Digits and tens/ones picture work are written out in words; place value of numbers above 99 is left to other standards.
notes.NC17.1.NBT.3: Numbers stay within two digits; the symbol is recorded in number sentences because a symbol cannot be chosen in a four-option list without a fourth meaningless option.
notes.NC17.1.NBT.4: All sums within 100. Models (tens rods, ones cubes, bundles) are written out in words. Explaining reasoning is tested by choosing the correct way or finishing a described strategy.
notes.NC17.1.NBT.5: All numbers and answers stay within 100 (the standard covers two-digit numbers); the only answer of 100 is 10 more than 90.
notes.NC17.1.NBT.6: Minuends 10 to 90 only, differences 0 to 80, tens subtracted from tens. Models are written as rods of ten, number lines as jumps of tens. Skills: tens from a multiple of 10, rods of ten, count back on a number line, story problems, explain the tens reasoning, compare and match differences.
notes.NC17.1.MD.1: Grade 1 lengths are compared without numbers of units (that is 1.MD.2). Questions use word statements, three or four objects, and a third object (string, rope, stick) for indirect comparison. Numeric answers are counts or a place in an order (1, 2 or 3).
notes.NC17.1.MD.2: Grade 1: all lengths are whole numbers of units, within 20; no question uses a ruler or a picture. A few later questions use the idea that a shorter unit needs more copies; "end to end with no gaps or overlaps" is tested in words.
notes.NC17.1.MD.3: Grade 1: clocks are given in words (hand positions, digital times), never pictures. Half past times are always described with the short hand between two numbers, so the description is true. Time answers are digital choice options (a time cannot be a numeric answer); numeric questions ask for an hour, a hand number, a minute count or a count of clocks. No questions on elapsed time or minutes other than :00 and :30.
notes.NC17.1.MD.5: Grade 1: coins are named and valued only by name (penny 1, nickel 5, dime 10, quarter 25 cents), never shown. Everything is related to pennies, as the summary asks; sums of mixed coins are Grade 2 and left out. Same-coin amounts stay within 50 pennies. Coins are not told apart by size, since no picture is shown.
notes.NC17.1.MD.4: Grade 1: data in up to three categories is written out as a list or counts; totals stay within 20. No picture graph is used. Organising (sorting and counting a written list) is tested in the sort-a-list questions.
notes.NC17.1.G.1: Thirty questions in words only: defining and non-defining attributes (color, size, direction, material), naming flat and solid shapes from attributes, counting sides and corners, and building with straws. Drawing is tested by what a student would draw, since a canvas cannot be used here. Solid shapes are limited to cube, cone, cylinder and sphere.
notes.NC17.1.G.2: Shapes are described in words. Counts of sides and corners are of the outside of the joined shape, and each stem fixes how the shapes are joined so there is one answer. No fractions beyond halves are used (halves of a circle).
notes.NC17.1.G.3: Circles and rectangles are described in words; no pictures. Questions stay on halves, fourths/quarters, equal shares and "more shares are smaller".

questions.skill: Name a coin from its value

questions.skill: Most and least

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer

questions.skill: Most and least

questions.solution: The numbers are 8, 3 and 6. 3 is the least, so there are the fewest balls.

solve.work: Balls 3 is less than blocks 6 and cars 8.

questions.skill: Read the count of one category

questions.solution: Find Duck in the list. It says 4, so 4 ducks were seen.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer

questions.solution: Stars and hearts both have 6. The moons have 3, which is different.

questions.skill: Sort a list into categories and count
questions.stem: Lena wrote down what 10 children ate for lunch: pizza, soup, pizza, salad, soup, pizza, pizza, salad, soup, pizza. How many children ate pizza?
questions.solution: Count the word pizza in the list. It is the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th and 10th lunch. That is 5 children.

questions.skill: Sort a list into categories and count

solve.work: red at 1,5 = 2; blue at 2,3,6,8 = 4; green at 4,7 = 2. Total 8.

questions.skill: Total of all the categories

questions.solution: Add all three: 8 + 5 + 4 = 17. There are 17 pieces of fruit.

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer

questions.skill: Compare categories: how many more or fewer

There are 3 more cars than trucks
There are 4 more cars than trucks
There are 4 more buses than cars
questions.answer: There are 4 more cars than trucks
questions.solution: 9 - 5 = 4, so there are 4 more cars than trucks. The other sentences do not match the numbers.

solve.answer: There are 4 more cars than trucks
solve.work: Cars 9 - trucks 5 = 4 more cars than trucks. Buses are fewer than cars; trucks fewer than cars.

questions.skill: Most and least

questions.skill: Find a missing count from the total

questions.skill: Combine categories

questions.solution: The numbers are 6, 11 and 4. The greatest is 11, the blue hats.

questions.solution: Add all three groups: 5 + 7 + 4 = 16. Mark has 16 stickers.

questions.stem: Mia puts 2 squares next to each other. They are the same size. They touch along one whole side. What new shape do they make?
questions.solution: The two squares make a long shape. It has 4 sides and 4 square corners, and it is longer than it is tall. That is a rectangle, not a square.

solve.work: Two equal squares joined along a whole side make a shape twice as long as it is wide: a rectangle.

questions.skill: Make a flat shape from simpler flat shapes
questions.stem: Ben has 2 half-circles that are the same size. He puts their straight sides together. What shape does he make?
questions.solution: A circle cut through the middle gives 2 half-circles. Putting the straight sides back together makes the circle again.

solve.work: Two equal half-circles joined along their straight sides (diameters) make a whole circle.

questions.skill: Make solid shapes by joining or stacking
questions.stem: Lin stacks 2 cans, one on top of the other. The cans are cylinders of the same size. What solid shape is the tall stack?
questions.solution: Two same-size cylinders stacked make a taller cylinder. It still has 2 flat circles and one curved side.

solve.work: Two equal cylinders stacked end to end make a taller cylinder.

questions.skill: Take a composite shape apart into simpler shapes
questions.stem: Dan cuts a square paper from one corner to the opposite corner with one straight cut. He gets 2 pieces. How many triangles does he get?
questions.solution: The straight cut from corner to corner makes 2 pieces. Each piece has 3 sides, so each is a triangle. Dan gets 2 triangles.

solve.work: A diagonal cut of a square gives 2 pieces, each a triangle. 2.

questions.skill: Name the parts of a composite shape (sides, corners, faces)
questions.stem: A rectangle is made from 2 squares. How many corners does the rectangle have?
questions.solution: Count the corners of the rectangle only, not the corners where the squares touch inside. A rectangle has 4 corners.

solve.work: A rectangle has 4 corners (the inner meeting points of the squares are not corners of the rectangle).

questions.skill: Take a composite shape apart into simpler shapes
questions.stem: Ana cuts a circle into 2 equal parts. She cuts through the middle. What is each part?
questions.solution: Cutting a circle through the middle makes 2 equal parts. Each part is a half-circle.

solve.work: Cutting a circle through the centre into 2 equal parts gives two half-circles.

questions.skill: Make a flat shape from simpler flat shapes
questions.stem: Jo has 2 triangles that are the same size. Each triangle has 1 square corner and 2 sides that are the same length. Which shape can Jo make with them?
questions.solution: Put the two longest sides together. The two triangles fit to make a square. A circle needs curved sides, and a cube and a cone are solid shapes.

solve.work: Two equal right isosceles triangles joined along their long sides make a square. Cone, cube are solids; circle impossible.

questions.skill: Name and count the shapes a composite shape is made from
questions.stem: Gus makes a square from 2 triangles. Then he makes another square the same way. How many triangles does he use in all?
questions.solution: Each square needs 2 triangles. For 2 squares: 2 + 2 = 4 triangles.

questions.skill: Name and count the shapes a composite shape is made from
questions.stem: Fay draws a tree. The top is a triangle. The bottom is a tall rectangle. Which 2 shapes make the tree?
choices: A circle and a big triangle
questions.solution: The tree has a triangle on the top and a rectangle on the bottom, so it is made from a triangle and a rectangle.

solve.work: Top triangle, bottom rectangle: a triangle and a rectangle.

questions.skill: Name and count the shapes a composite shape is made from
questions.stem: A rocket picture is made from flat shapes. The body is a rectangle. The nose is a triangle. There is also a triangle on each side. How many triangles are in the rocket?
questions.solution: There is 1 triangle for the nose and 1 triangle on each side. That is 1 + 2 = 3 triangles.

solve.work: Nose 1 triangle + 1 on each of 2 sides = 3 triangles.

questions.skill: Make solid shapes by joining or stacking
questions.stem: Ruth builds a toy rocket. She puts a cone on top of a cylinder. Which solid shapes does she use?
questions.solution: The top of the rocket is a cone and the body is a cylinder. She uses a cone and a cylinder.

solve.work: A cone on top of a cylinder: a cone and a cylinder.

questions.skill: Make solid shapes by joining or stacking
questions.stem: Sam builds a tower with cubes. The bottom layer has 4 cubes. The top layer has 3 cubes. How many cubes does he use?
questions.solution: Add the two layers: 4 + 3 = 7 cubes.

questions.skill: Name and count the shapes a composite shape is made from
questions.stem: A house picture is made from flat shapes. The walls are 1 big square. The roof is 1 triangle. The door is 1 tall thin rectangle. The 2 windows are small squares. How many squares are in the picture?
questions.solution: Count the squares: 1 big square for the walls and 2 small squares for the windows. That is 1 + 2 = 3 squares.

solve.work: Walls 1 big square + 2 window squares = 3 squares (door is a rectangle, roof a triangle).

questions.skill: Name the parts of a composite shape (sides, corners, faces)
questions.stem: Two cubes are glued together to make a rectangular prism. How many faces does the rectangular prism have?
questions.solution: A rectangular prism has 6 faces. Gluing makes one solid shape, so we count the faces of the new shape, not 6 + 6.

solve.work: Two cubes glued face to face make a rectangular prism, which has 6 faces.

questions.skill: Take a composite shape apart into simpler shapes
questions.stem: Pia has a rectangle made from 2 squares that are the same size. She cuts along the line where the squares meet. What shape is each piece?
questions.solution: Cutting along the line where they meet takes the rectangle back to the 2 squares. Each piece is a square.

solve.work: Cutting along the shared line separates the two squares: each piece is a square.

questions.skill: Make a flat shape from simpler flat shapes
questions.stem: Bea has 4 small squares that are the same size. She puts them in 2 rows of 2. They touch along whole sides. What shape do they make?
questions.solution: 2 rows of 2 makes a shape that is as wide as it is tall, with 4 square corners. It is a bigger square.

solve.work: 2 rows of 2 equal squares make a bigger square (2 by 2).

questions.skill: Name the parts of a composite shape (sides, corners, faces)
questions.stem: Tara puts a triangle on top of a square. All 3 sides of the triangle are the same length as a side of the square. One side of the triangle fits exactly on the top side of the square. How many sides does the new shape have?
questions.solution: The square has 4 sides, but its top side is now covered. The sides left are 3 from the square. The triangle adds 2 sides on top. That is 3 + 2 = 5 sides.

solve.work: Equilateral triangle on the top of the square: outline has bottom, 2 square sides, 2 triangle sides = 5 (no sides line up since 60+90 is not 180).

questions.skill: Make solid shapes by joining or stacking
questions.stem: Jo glues 3 cubes in a row, face to face. What solid shape does she make?
questions.solution: Three cubes in a row make a long block. It has 6 flat faces that are rectangles. It is a rectangular prism, not a cube.

solve.work: 3 cubes in a row face to face: a rectangular prism (3 by 1 by 1).

questions.skill: Name and count the shapes a composite shape is made from
questions.stem: A flower picture is made from 1 circle in the middle and 6 half-circles around it. How many shapes are in the flower?
questions.solution: Add the circle and the half-circles: 1 + 6 = 7 shapes.

questions.skill: Name the parts of a composite shape
questions.stem: Sue joins 3 squares in a row to make a long rectangle. The squares are the same size. How many of the squares touch the middle square along a whole side?
questions.solution: The middle square has one square on its left and one square on its right. That is 2 squares.

solve.work: Squares in a row: left, middle, right. The middle square shares one whole side with the left square and one whole side with the right square. So 2 squares touch it along a whole side.

questions.skill: Make a flat shape from simpler flat shapes
questions.stem: Rob puts 6 triangles around one point. The triangles are the same size, and all 3 sides of each triangle are the same length. They touch along whole sides with no gaps. What shape do they make?
questions.solution: The 6 triangles make a ring with 6 outside sides. A shape with 6 sides is a hexagon.

solve.work: Six equal equilateral triangles around a point (6 x 60 = 360) make a hexagon.

questions.skill: Name the parts of a composite shape (sides, corners, faces)
questions.stem: Five squares are joined to make a plus sign. One square is in the middle. One more square is on each of its 4 sides. How many corners does the plus sign have?
questions.solution: Walk around the outside of the plus sign and count each turn. There are 12 corners.

solve.work: Plus sign outline is a 12-sided polygon; each of the 4 arms contributes 2 outer corners and there are 4 inner corners: 8+4 = 12.

questions.skill: Make a flat shape from simpler flat shapes
questions.stem: Kit has 2 rectangles that are the same size. Each is 2 inches wide and 4 inches long. She puts them together so the 4-inch sides touch. What shape does she make?
choices: A square that is 4 inches on each side
A rectangle 2 inches wide and 8 inches long
A circle that is 4 inches across
A triangle with sides of 4 inches
questions.answer: A square that is 4 inches on each side
questions.solution: The new shape is 2 + 2 = 4 inches wide and still 4 inches long. All 4 sides are 4 inches, so it is a square.

solve.answer: A square that is 4 inches on each side
solve.work: Each rectangle is 2 by 4. Joining along the 4-inch sides puts them side by side: width 2+2 = 4, length 4. A 4 by 4 square.

questions.skill: Take a composite shape apart into simpler shapes
questions.stem: Lee has a row of 5 squares joined side by side. He cuts them apart along the lines where they touch. Each cut separates one piece into two pieces. How many cuts does he make to get 5 single squares?
questions.solution: There are 4 places where two squares touch. Each needs 1 cut, so Lee makes 4 cuts.

solve.work: 5 squares in a row have 4 shared lines; each cut adds one piece: 1 to 5 pieces needs 4 cuts.

questions.skill: Make solid shapes by joining or stacking
questions.stem: Jo builds a block from 10 cubes. It has 2 layers, and each layer has the same number of cubes. How many cubes are in each layer?
questions.solution: Split 10 cubes into 2 equal layers: 5 + 5 = 10. Each layer has 5 cubes.

questions.skill: Make solid shapes by joining or stacking
questions.stem: Tia builds with cubes. The bottom layer has 2 rows with 3 cubes in each row. The top layer has 1 row of 3 cubes. How many cubes does she use?
questions.solution: The bottom layer has 3 + 3 = 6 cubes. The top layer has 3 cubes. Together: 6 + 3 = 9 cubes.

questions.skill: Make a flat shape from simpler flat shapes
questions.stem: Pam puts 2 triangles together to make a square. Then she puts 2 of those squares side by side, touching along one whole side. What shape does she make?
questions.solution: Two squares side by side make a long shape with 4 sides and 4 square corners. That is a rectangle.

solve.work: Two squares side by side along a whole side make a rectangle.

questions.skill: Take a composite shape apart into simpler shapes
questions.stem: A rectangle is made from 2 rows of 3 squares. Pia cuts it along the line between the two rows. How many squares are in each piece?
questions.solution: The rectangle has 3 + 3 = 6 squares. The cut makes 2 equal pieces with 3 squares each.

solve.work: 2 rows of 3 squares, cut between rows: each piece is one row of 3 squares.

questions.skill: Name the parts of a composite shape (sides, corners, faces)
questions.stem: Ruth has a square and 2 triangles. All 3 sides of each triangle are as long as a side of the square. She puts one triangle exactly on the top side of the square and the other exactly on the bottom side. How many straight sides does the new shape have?
questions.solution: The left and right sides of the square stay: 2 sides. The top triangle adds 2 sides and the bottom triangle adds 2 sides. That is 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 sides.

solve.work: Square with equilateral triangles on top and bottom: 2 left/right square sides + 2 sides of each triangle = 6 sides (no sides line up).

questions.skill: Name equal shares as halves or fourths
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 2 equal shares. What is each share called?
questions.solution: A whole cut into 2 equal shares has two halves. Each share is a half.

solve.work: 2 equal shares: each is a half.

questions.skill: Name equal shares as halves or fourths
questions.stem: Which word means 1 of 4 equal shares?
questions.solution: 4 equal shares are called fourths, so 1 of them is a fourth. A quarter means the same thing.

solve.work: 1 of 4 equal shares is a fourth.

questions.skill: Tell equal shares from unequal pieces
questions.stem: Which is a way to cut a circle into halves?
choices: Into 2 pieces that are the same size
Into 2 pieces, one bigger than the other
Into 4 pieces that are the same size
Into 3 pieces that are the same size
questions.answer: Into 2 pieces that are the same size
questions.solution: Halves are 2 equal shares, so the 2 pieces must be the same size. Cutting into 4 pieces makes fourths.

solve.answer: Into 2 pieces that are the same size

questions.skill: Name equal shares as halves or fourths
questions.stem: Which word means the same as fourth?
questions.solution: Fourth and quarter are two names for 1 of 4 equal shares.

solve.work: A fourth is also called a quarter.

questions.skill: Name equal shares as halves or fourths
questions.stem: Dad cuts a pancake into 2 equal parts and gives 1 part to Lily. What part of the pancake does Lily get?
questions.solution: The pancake was cut into 2 equal parts. Lily gets 1 of them, which is a half.

solve.work: 1 of 2 equal parts is a half.

questions.skill: Count the equal shares in a whole
questions.stem: A pie is cut into halves. How many equal shares is that?
questions.solution: Halves are 2 equal shares.

questions.skill: Count the equal shares in a whole
questions.stem: Mia cuts a rectangle of paper into fourths. How many pieces does she have?
questions.solution: Fourths are 4 equal shares, so Mia has 4 pieces.

questions.skill: A whole is made of its shares
questions.stem: How many halves make 1 whole pizza?
questions.solution: A pizza cut into halves has 2 equal shares, so 2 halves make 1 whole.

questions.skill: A whole is made of its shares
questions.stem: Tom has 1 whole cracker. How many quarters make the whole cracker?
questions.solution: A quarter is 1 of 4 equal shares, so 4 quarters make the whole cracker.

questions.skill: Count the equal shares in a whole
questions.stem: Cut a circle with 1 straight cut through the middle into equal shares. How many shares are there?
questions.solution: One cut across the middle makes 2 equal shares, which are halves.

solve.work: One straight cut through the middle makes 2 equal shares.

questions.skill: Tell equal shares from unequal pieces
questions.stem: Sam cuts a sandwich into 2 pieces. One piece is much bigger than the other. Are the pieces halves?
choices: Yes, because halves can be any size
No, halves must be equal shares
questions.answer: No, halves must be equal shares
questions.solution: Halves are 2 EQUAL shares. These pieces are not the same size, so they are not halves.

solve.answer: No, halves must be equal shares
solve.work: Halves must be equal; unequal pieces are not halves.

questions.skill: Name equal shares as halves or fourths
questions.stem: Lena makes 2 straight cuts across the middle of a round pie. She gets 4 pieces that are the same size. What is each piece called?
questions.solution: 4 equal shares are fourths. Each piece is a fourth of the pie.

solve.work: 4 equal pieces: each is a fourth.

questions.skill: More equal shares make smaller shares
questions.stem: Two pizzas are the same size. Pizza A is cut into 2 equal shares. Pizza B is cut into 4 equal shares. Which pizza has the smaller shares?
choices: Both have the same size shares
questions.solution: Both pizzas are the same size, but Pizza B is cut into more shares, so each of its shares is smaller.

solve.work: Same-size pizzas: more shares means smaller shares, so Pizza B (fourths).

questions.skill: More equal shares make smaller shares
questions.stem: A pie is cut into halves. A pie of the same size is cut into fourths. Which is bigger?
questions.solution: When the same size whole is cut into fewer shares, each share is bigger. A half is bigger than a fourth.

solve.work: A half of a pie is bigger than a fourth of a same-size pie.

questions.skill: Name equal shares as halves or fourths
questions.stem: Ben shares a rectangle cake with his sister. They each get an equal share. What part of the cake does each one get?
questions.solution: 2 people share equally, so the cake is cut into 2 equal shares. Each share is a half.

solve.work: 2 people share equally: each gets a half.

questions.skill: Shares left after some are used
questions.stem: A sandwich is cut into fourths. Dad eats 1 fourth. How many fourths are left?
questions.solution: The sandwich has 4 fourths. Take away 1: 4 - 1 = 3.

questions.skill: Count shares across several wholes
questions.stem: Ann and Ben each get 1 half of a pie. Cy and Di each get 1 half of another pie of the same size. How many halves are given out in all?
questions.solution: Ann and Ben have 2 halves. Cy and Di have 2 halves. 2 + 2 = 4 halves.

questions.skill: Shares left after some are used
questions.stem: Four friends will share a pizza equally. It is cut into fourths. 3 friends have taken their fourth. How many fourths are left?
questions.solution: There are 4 fourths. 3 have been taken. 4 - 3 = 1.

questions.skill: Shares left after some are used
questions.stem: Sue has a cake cut into fourths. She has eaten 2 of them. How many fourths are left?
questions.solution: The cake has 4 fourths. 4 - 2 = 2.

questions.skill: More equal shares make smaller shares
questions.stem: One pizza is cut into halves. Another pizza of the same size is cut into fourths. How many more shares does the second pizza have than the first?
questions.solution: The first pizza has 2 shares and the second has 4. 4 - 2 = 2 more.

questions.skill: Cut shares again into equal shares
questions.stem: Mark cuts a paper rectangle into 2 equal shares. Then he cuts each share into 2 equal shares. What are the 4 new shares called?
questions.solution: The rectangle is now cut into 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are fourths.

solve.work: 2 shares each cut into 2 equal shares gives 4 equal shares of the whole: fourths.

questions.skill: More equal shares make smaller shares
questions.stem: Which sentence is true about the same sandwich cut into halves and cut into fourths?
choices: A fourth is bigger than a half
A fourth is the same size as a half
A fourth is smaller than a half
A fourth is the whole sandwich
questions.answer: A fourth is smaller than a half
questions.solution: Cutting into 4 shares gives smaller shares than cutting into 2. So a fourth is smaller than a half.

solve.answer: A fourth is smaller than a half
solve.work: Fourths are smaller than halves of the same whole.

questions.skill: More equal shares make smaller shares
questions.stem: Jo says, "If I cut a cake into more equal shares, each share gets bigger." Is Jo right?
choices: No, the shares stay the same size
questions.solution: The same cake is split into more pieces, so each piece must be smaller.

solve.work: More equal shares of the same cake makes each share smaller, so Jo is wrong.

questions.skill: A whole is made of its shares
questions.stem: Tia says a whole pizza is 4 fourths. Which is another way to say a whole pizza?
questions.solution: A pizza cut into 2 equal shares has 2 halves, and together they are the whole pizza. 2 fourths is only part of a pizza.

questions.skill: Tell equal shares from unequal pieces
questions.stem: Ben wants to share a rectangle cake equally with 3 friends, so 4 people in all. How should he cut it, and what is each share?
choices: Into 4 equal shares; each is a fourth
Into 2 equal shares; each is a fourth
Into 4 equal shares; each is a half
Into 4 shares of different sizes; each is a fourth
questions.answer: Into 4 equal shares; each is a fourth
questions.solution: 4 people sharing equally need 4 equal shares. Each share is a fourth.

solve.answer: Into 4 equal shares; each is a fourth
solve.work: 4 people: cut into 4 equal shares, each a fourth.

questions.skill: Cut shares again into equal shares
questions.stem: Zed cuts a square sandwich into halves. Then he cuts each half into 2 equal shares. How many equal shares are there now?
questions.solution: There are 2 halves, and each is cut into 2 shares: 2 + 2 = 4 shares.

questions.skill: Count shares across several wholes
questions.stem: Zoe has 2 sandwiches that are the same size. She cuts each one into fourths. How many fourths does she have in all?
questions.solution: Each sandwich has 4 fourths. 4 + 4 = 8.

questions.skill: Count shares across several wholes
questions.stem: Kai has 2 pies cut into halves and 1 pie cut into fourths. How many shares are there in all?
questions.solution: The two pies have 2 + 2 = 4 halves. The other pie has 4 fourths. 4 + 4 = 8 shares.

questions.skill: Count shares across several wholes
questions.stem: A baker cuts 3 pies into fourths. How many fourths does the baker have?
questions.solution: Each pie has 4 fourths. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

questions.skill: Count shares across several wholes
questions.stem: A teacher has 5 circles of paper. She cuts every circle into halves. How many halves does she have?
questions.solution: Each circle makes 2 halves. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.
